neighbours.caption: Electron micrograph of part of a glomerular basement membrane in the renal biopsy specimen from the woman of 28 with hereditary nephropathy of Alport type, which is illustrated in 9.10. This is at the same magnification as the normal basement membrane in 6.6 and the thin basement membrane in 9.9. The basement membrane has an irregular outer aspect, variable width with thick and thin areas, splitting of the lamina densa, and small inclusions

Electron micrograph showing a tubulo-reticular body in a glomerular endothelial cell. This is frequently found in HIV infection, but is also seen in other conditions, such as lupus nephritis, which is the diagnosis in this renal biopsy specimen, from a woman of 37 with proteinuria
wire loops seen by light microscopy; subendothelial dense deposits; subendothelial dense deposits correspond to wire loops seen by light microscopy

Electron micrograph of part of a glomerulus in a renal biopsy specimen from a man of 37, with HIV infection and the nephrotic syndrome. There are microtubular structures in the mesangium, indicating immunotactoid glomerulopathy

Electron micrograph of glomerular basement membranes in a renal biopsy specimen from a woman of 28 with persistent microscopic hematuria and proteinuria. Her brother was on renal replacement therapy, but the cause of his renal failure was not known. The membranes have an irregular outer aspect, a range of thickness, and splitting of the lamina densa. These are features of hereditary nephropathy of Alport type.

full.description: This is an electron micrograph of a renal biopsy specimen. It shows a tubulo-reticular body within a glomerular endothelial cell. Such structures are frequently found in HIV infection, but may also be seen in other conditions like lupus nephritis. The image reveals characteristic microtubular or reticular inclusions in the cell's cytoplasm.

random.description: This image is a transmission electron micrograph showing intracellular viral or structural components. It displays two circular, concentric viral capsids enclosed within a membrane-bound vacuole or envelope. The ultrastructural morphology is consistent with a viral infection, such as herpesvirus or a similar pathogen, inside a host cell. Further correlation with clinical history would be required for a definitive diagnosis.
